The packet still breaks inside the owner and the fixture entry points. I will read those ranges in the checkout and check the authority, allocation, and cleanup paths.**CLEAR**

Reviewed commit `d78b7b189e100ab6b3260b497d67449ee29e031c` in this checkout, read-only, against the B2 connection scope. No tests, compilers, Docker, or CI were run. This is not physical D15 qualification, local positive-compiler execution, B1/B3/B4 closure, milestone acceptance, archive, or merge approval. Hosted CI `40313370100` at this commit stays pending.

No blocking correctness, security, custody, or resource defect in the connection.

Shared authority is `_compiler_authority_v1` (`accepted_policy_fixture_compiler_v1.py` 1404–1471). `preflight_fixture_engine_v1` (1523–1554) and `_compile_fixture_owned_v1` (1569–1570) both call it with `usable=True`, so whole-chain scope, sealed qualification, expiry, foreign root, and source binding are one policy. Expiry and schema failure happen before helper reads, disk floors, `/proc` identity, output mkdir, and `_DockerClientV1` (1690–1691). The owner still caps the deadline at 150s and still requires more than 80s of containment room (1416–1417).

All three fixture entry points refuse before fixture allocations. `preflight_original_fixture_engine_v1` (123–140) rejects a missing qualification, admission, or non-int deadline before `build_fixture_source_v1`, then calls the shared preflight before returning bytes. `prepare_original_fixture_engine_v1` (182–196) mkdirs and writes only after that preflight. `prepared_complete_fixture_inputs_v1` (68–73) and `v2` (114–122) do the same before `output.mkdir`, `/var/tmp` mkdtemp, and sockets. v2’s reply-map checks run first and do not create those resources. The same `absolute_deadline_ns` is passed into every `_compiler_preparation_clock_v1` call and into `compile_fixture_engine_v1` (198–200). That clock (1514–1519) refuses a non-positive or greater-than-150s window and does not extend it.

`_write_fixture_source_v1` (143–172) keeps the first write, flush, fsync, or short-write cause and a later close or deadline cause. The hold cleanup (230–248) closes the socket and the ELF fd, merges those causes onto `FixtureCompilerError`, and leaves any other initiating exception in place with `fixture_cleanup_causes`.

The genuine compiler file has no `cc`, `subprocess`, or `shutil` fallback. Container limits, tmpfs, CORE/fsize, ELF ABI, and channel checks remain on the owner path (1744–1803). `controlled_fixture_compiler_v1` is imported only by the two real-ELF test modules. It patches `preflight_fixture_engine_v1` and `compile_fixture_engine_v1` only inside its context, uses `/usr/bin/cc` only there, and returns `controlled_test_only: True` and `physical_qualification: False`. Those tests still call the real default image/probe readers and the real custody capture. Preflight and transport tests add no skip. The existing `linux` and `cc` skip remains only on the two real-ELF classes.

Residual limits, not change requests: a failure after `mkdtemp` in the physical fixtures can leave a mode-0700 `/var/tmp` directory, because those finally blocks only close sockets. Missing, malformed, expired, and foreign authority return before that `mkdtemp`. The three positive controlled-compiler tests remain unexecuted by this review.
